diff_ref: git diff 28da8a0f..a9e6e0e1 -- scripts/generate_spine.py tests/test_generate_spine.py specs/implementer.spine.toml specs/reviewer.spine.toml .agent-work/epic-559/c2-generate-the-spine/dispatch-proof/probe.spine.toml (the rework round: Blockers 0/1/2/4 + source-fixed divergence)

smells.finding: New/changed functions stay bounded: _numeric_field_faults ~13 lines, _probe_pytest_not_yet_written ~35 lines of body (docstring is long but body is a single early-return plus one subprocess call), compile_condition's new elif branch adds ~15 lines to a function that is still ~38 lines total. No new nesting level introduced.
Module is function-based (no classes); Undecidable gained one field (blocking: bool = True), not new responsibility.

The diff actively REMOVES a duplication risk: _run_pytest_collect was extracted out of the old inline _probe_pytest body so both _probe_pytest and the new _probe_pytest_not_yet_written share one subprocess-invocation site instead of two copies of the same pytest --collect-only command construction.
All new functions operate on dicts/values they receive as parameters (cond, spec) and return faults/undecidables; no reach-into another module's internals.
_numeric_field_faults(where, cond, *fields) takes a varargs field list rather than repeating (where, cond, field) triples at each of the 2 call sites -- the opposite of a clump.

not_yet_written is a bool flag on the condition dict, matching the existing convention for other kind-specific optional fields (e.g. min_collect, targets) already in this same dict shape -- not a new primitive-typing pattern.

_run_pytest_collect(selector, targets, *, repo_root) and _probe_pytest_not_yet_written(gid, cid, cond, *, repo_root) both match the existing _probe_pytest(gid, cid, cond, *, repo_root) signature shape already used elsewhere in the module -- 3-4 params, keyword-only repo_root.

The behavior change is concentrated in one file (scripts/generate_spine.py) plus its one test file; the two shipped spec fixes (specs/implementer.spine.toml, specs/reviewer.spine.toml) are each a single-line placeholder swap with no code-shape change, and the dispatch-proof spec fix is a single args-list addition. No scatter across unrelated modules.

_cond_faults and compile_condition already dispatch on `kind` (population/pytest/script/artifact/qualitative) before this round; the rework adds one more axis (a numeric-type check, a not_yet_written branch) to concerns those functions already own, rather than bolting on an unrelated new reason to change either function.
No chained attribute/dict access beyond direct one-level cond.get(...)/spec.get(...) lookups.

_numeric_field_faults(where, cond, *fields) is a varargs helper, but it already has 2 real call sites in this same diff (population's 3 fields, pytest's 1 field) -- per the deep-module vocabulary doctrine ('one adapter = a hypothetical seam; two = a real one'), 2 call sites make this a real, not speculative, generalization.

New comments explain non-obvious WHY (why check:null was the only buildable shape given validate_spine.validate()'s unconditional zero-collect re-probe; why bool is excluded from the numeric-field check despite isinstance(True,int) being True; why shipped_spec_session_specific_parent_faults is deliberately not wired into spec_shape_faults) -- removing them would lose real constraints a future reader needs, not restate what the code already says.
